buttonLabel: "Explore festival tours through Brazil and Bolivia"
lead: >-
  On the current festive itineraries through Brazil and Bolivia, the main event takes place in Rio de Janeiro: Carnival and the Champions' Parade, or New Year's Eve on Copacabana. The Bolivian days focus on the Altiplano lagoons, Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz and Tiwanaku. The choice depends on the festival date, Sambadrome tickets, transfers and the abrupt change in conditions from coastal Rio to the highlands.
---

## Events and festivals on journeys through Brazil and Bolivia

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through Brazil and Bolivia as part of longer journeys. **The actual festive event on these itineraries takes place in Brazil**, primarily in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The Bolivian section is a high-altitude journey through lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) Salt Flat, [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and archaeological sites.

The combination "Brazil + Bolivia: Events and Festivals" should therefore not be taken as a promise to attend a carnival in each country. None of the three tours includes a festival in Bolivia. Their appeal lies elsewhere: after an exciting night at the Sambadrome or on New Year's Eve, the journey continues to landscapes that would be difficult to combine with Rio on a short holiday.

For every route involving these countries, start with the [general Brazil + Bolivia selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil/). To compare festive events across other country combinations, see the [multi-country event travel catalog](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## Carnival in Rio: the main parades and Champions' Parade

[Rio de Janeiro Carnival](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) is especially renowned for the samba schools performing at the Sambadrome. Grandstands, percussion ensembles, floats and costumes create an elaborate overnight spectacle. However, **the main competitive parades and the separate Champions' Parade are different events on the calendar**. When booking a tour, you need to match its specific carnival night to your arrival date.

On [the 18-day itinerary featuring the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), the first days are spent in Rio. Day two includes a city tour, Sugarloaf Mountain and the evening Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome. The published inclusions specify a ticket in Sector 9 or a comparable sector and a hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfer. It is a long night: the program explicitly allows participants to leave before the parade ends.

[The 19-day five-country Carnival itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) is structured differently. It begins with an overview of Rio, with the third day devoted to Carnival. An evening transfer to the Sambadrome is planned, followed by a return to the hotel after the overnight parade; another day is dedicated to Corcovado. Tickets for the Champions' Parade are also listed among this tour's services, so when agreeing on the dates, it is important to establish **which exact night and ticket are confirmed for your departure**.

If you specifically want to see the Champions' Parade, the first itinerary is the clearest choice because the event is explicitly named in its title and a particular day. Carnival events and parade calendars change from year to year; dates from one season should never be carried over to another.

## New Year's Eve on Copacabana: a very different celebration

[The 19-day five-country New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) begins in Rio on December 30. On **December 31**, after visiting Corcovado, the program includes celebrating New Year's Eve on Copacabana. The celebration brings together the oceanfront, fireworks, city music and the tradition of dressing in white.

This is quite different from the Carnival Sambadrome. The main experience is **celebrating on a city beach**, not watching a competition of samba schools from the stands. January 1 is devoted to Sugarloaf Mountain and a city tour, followed by free time in Rio. That schedule is helpful after a late New Year's night.

The Brazilian portion of this New Year itinerary continues to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The journey then runs through Argentina and Chile to Bolivia. The entire 19-day tour should not be described as "New Year in Bolivia": the celebration takes place in Rio, while the Bolivian segment contains regular nature excursions according to the published itinerary.

For other festive programs, see [event-focused tours involving Brazil](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/) and [routes involving Bolivia](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/bolivia/). The selection is based on the whole tour, so in each case check the country and day of the actual event.

## What awaits in Bolivia after the celebrations

On all three itineraries, the Bolivian leg starts after Chile, from the [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) area, and crosses the highlands. The highlights here are lagoons, volcanic scenery, days traveling by four-wheel drive and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Next come [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and Tiwanaku, after which the journey continues to Peru.

**None of these segments lists a visit to Bolivian Carnival or a specially organized local festival.** The festive experience has already taken place in Brazil. In Bolivia, travelers face different weather, altitude and physical demands, so elegant clothes and lightweight Rio outfits are no substitute for warm clothing on the Altiplano.

Uyuni can be in its rainy season during the South American summer. Water on the salt flat sometimes produces a mirror-like surface, but it can also affect whether off-road vehicles can access particular areas. Neither a guaranteed "mirror" nor unrestricted access to every stop can be promised. The route and access to individual sites are reviewed according to the season and actual conditions.

Altitude is another important consideration. After relatively low-lying cities and waterfalls, the journey climbs into the Bolivian highlands. Discuss this transition in advance when planning the pace, breaks and individual health limitations; festivities in Rio do not reduce the strain of the subsequent long drives.

## Comparing festive itineraries

| Program | Main event |
|---|---|
| [5 countries, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Champions' Parade in Rio |
| [5 countries, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Carnival days in Rio |
| [New Year, 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) | December 31 on Copacabana |

Choose the **Champions' Parade** to see the samba schools perform after the main competitive part of Carnival. Compare **the other Carnival program** by the exact day and Sambadrome ticket category. **New Year** suits those who want to celebrate beside the ocean before taking a long journey to Uyuni and Machu Picchu.

All three journeys include considerably more than two countries: Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. None is a self-contained uninterrupted itinerary limited to Brazil and Bolivia. A shortened route requires a new agreement on transport, number of days and included excursions.

## Planning flights, tickets and clothing

For Carnival, first establish **the exact date of the chosen parade** and the admission category at the Sambadrome. The Champions' Parade takes place separately from the main competitive nights. Arrivals, hotel check-ins and city transport during the festivities should allow for road closures and heavy demand in Rio. Tickets and transfers are specified in both Carnival programs, but actual dates and seats are confirmed at booking.

For New Year, the priorities differ: arriving before December 31, having time to rest after your flight and returning safely from Copacabana. Celebrating New Year's Eve on the beach should not be confused with holding a ticket for the Carnival Sambadrome; these are different experiences.

After the festivities, the journey involves flights between cities and travel on high-altitude roads. Your suitcase has to accommodate light Rio clothing, shoes for Iguazu and warm layers for Bolivia. When crossing borders, check travel documents, transit and visa requirements for your nationality, payment methods and local currencies. A single card or one country's cash cannot be guaranteed to work everywhere on the continent.

We can align the event dates with the start of your tour, transfers, journey length and pace after late-night celebrations. The sensible planning sequence is to confirm the event in Rio first, then the route through Argentina and Chile, and only afterward the conditions of high-altitude excursions in Bolivia. The [general Events and Festivals section](/interests/events-and-festivals/) introduces other formats, but tickets, departures and visits depend on the selected tour's itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours through Brazil and Bolivia

### Does Carnival take place in Bolivia on these tours?

The featured programs include festive events in Brazil, in Rio. The Bolivian days focus on the Altiplano, Uyuni, La Paz and cultural sites. No separate Bolivian Carnival visit is listed.

### Are the Champions' Parade and the main Carnival the same event?

No. The Champions' Parade takes place separately, after the competitive performances. It is explicitly listed in [the 18-day Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/); for other Carnival itineraries, check the exact date and ticket inclusions.

### Which tour is suitable for spending New Year's Eve on Copacabana?

[The 19-day New Year itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/). According to the program, December 31 is spent in Rio, with an evening celebration on Copacabana; the journey then continues through other countries to Bolivia and Peru.

### Will Uyuni have a mirror-like surface after the January celebration?

Reflections sometimes occur during the rainy season but depend on water levels and weather. The same conditions may prevent access to parts of the salt flat. A particular view or access to every location cannot be guaranteed.

### Can the itinerary be reduced to just Brazil and Bolivia?

That would require a separately planned sequence of flights and stops. The featured itineraries also have principal segments in Argentina, Chile and Peru; these cannot simply be removed without changing the route and included services.

### What should be chosen first: Carnival dates or flights?

First identify the exact parade or New Year's Eve in Rio, then coordinate international flights and the entire onward route. The date of the event is much less flexible than some sightseeing excursions.

buttonLabel: "Explore food and wine experiences in Bolivia and Brazil"
lead: >-
  Bolivia and Brazil appear together on a South American itinerary, but the culinary part of such a journey requires a closer look at the actual program. On the current six-country trip, Brazil is represented by Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu, while Bolivia features high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz. A separate wine-tasting excursion is offered in Chile, not in either of these two countries. We explain how to assess the time available for local cuisine, why a long itinerary is not automatically a food tour and which stops are best discussed when customizing a private journey.
---

## What does combining Bolivia and Brazil mean for a culinary journey?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Bolivia and Brazil among the main countries and gastronomy as one of the travel themes. **The gastronomy theme applies to the tour as a whole:** it does not in itself establish that a winery visit, cooking class or special tasting is scheduled in every country.

The current [six-country itinerary lasting 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), visits [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), then Argentina, Uruguay and Chile before crossing high-altitude Bolivia and continuing into Peru. Its program **specifically offers an optional excursion to the wineries of Chile's Maipo Valley**. No equivalent confirmed wine program appears in the Brazilian or Bolivian segments.

This distinction matters when choosing a trip: [the general Bolivia + Brazil combination](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil/) is suitable for exploring nature and cities, while wine enthusiasts should study the specific tasting day and its conditions.

## Brazil: urban cuisine between Rio and Iguazu

The Brazilian leg introduces travelers to Rio, its neighborhoods, panoramas from Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain, and then the tropical scenery of Iguazu. Restaurants and local dishes fit naturally into free time in Rio, but **this itinerary does not list an included gastronomic tour, cooking lesson or winery visit in Brazil**.

If local food is your main reason for traveling, it is better to discuss a specific format: time for lunch outside scheduled excursions, an interest in regional specialties, a preferred restaurant and transport to reach it. With a busy schedule in Rio and a flight to Iguazu, there is less free time than the number of days in the country might suggest.

For a different focus, explore [food and wine tours by interest](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [thematic itineraries through Brazil](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/brazil/), checking whether the specific activity is actually included in each itinerary.

## Bolivia: a high-altitude route and meals on the road

The Bolivian leg of the [20-day program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) passes through Altiplano lagoons, Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz and Tiwanaku. It is primarily the nature and history portion of a longer journey. One of the days near the salt flat includes a packed lunch; **this lunch should not be presented as a food excursion or tasting experience**.

During travel to remote high-altitude lagoons, meals depend on transfer times and the distance between stops. If you want a deeper introduction to Bolivian cuisine, it makes more sense to reserve time for restaurants in the cities than to expect them between salt flats and viewpoints. It is important to consider altitude, fatigue after long drives and access to drinking water. Dietary needs and travel limitations are agreed according to the group's composition.

See [routes through Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/) and [all gastronomic multi-country journeys](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) to distinguish a nature trip that offers opportunities to try local food from a program in which tastings are the main purpose.

## Where wine really appears on the current itinerary

**The confirmed wine activity is in Chile:** an optional excursion to Maipo Valley wineries with a tasting is offered on the day spent in Santiago. This is an extra-cost option, not an included service in Bolivia or Brazil.

If wine is the primary goal, consider what adding Chile offers: a dedicated thematic experience, but also a larger geographic scope and more transfers. If you want only two countries, a separate itinerary must be discussed; the existing six-country journey should not be treated as a continuous ready-made route through Bolivia and Brazil alone.

We can help establish priorities: preserve the nature days at Iguazu and Uyuni, allocate additional time for city restaurants or seek a program with confirmed tastings. The list of services, stop durations and cost of such adjustments are agreed separately.

## Assessing flights, altitude and expenses

The transition from Brazil's humid coast to high-altitude Bolivia brings a substantial change in travel conditions. Clothing and physical well-being require a different approach; parts of the journey take place at elevations that require acclimatization. Days involving long drives are best planned without obligatory evening events.

Bolivia and Brazil use different national currencies. Rather than promise that one card will work everywhere, check in advance which expenses the particular tour includes, how optional activities are paid for and which payment methods are available at each stop. Entry requirements depend on nationality and travel dates; there is no single rule for all passports.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about culinary journeys through Bolivia and Brazil

### Are wine tastings in both countries included in the selected itinerary?

No. The existing six-country tour lists an optional wine excursion in Chile's Maipo Valley. It does not include confirmed tastings in Bolivia or Brazil.

### Is this itinerary suitable for someone who wants to try local cuisine?

Yes, if the main goal is an extensive journey with opportunities to visit restaurants during free time. For a specialized food tour, choose a program explicitly listing markets, tastings or cooking activities.

### Can I visit only Bolivia and Brazil?

That would be a different itinerary. The current [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Peru. A private two-country combination would require a separate agreement on routes, flights and services.

### Where should I allow time for culinary stops?

In the urban portions of the itinerary, especially Rio and La Paz. The remote high-altitude segments primarily involve travel and natural sites; an included packed lunch does not replace a dedicated restaurant experience.

### How can I verify inclusions and prices without outdated figures?

Open [the specific itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and compare each day, included services and paid options. The total cost and duration shown in the selection are calculated from current program data, and optional tastings need to be budgeted separately.

buttonLabel: "Explore the nature of Bolivia and Brazil"
lead: "Brazilian waterfalls and forests contrast with the Uyuni Salt Flat and lagoons of Bolivia's Altiplano. We examine actual multi-country tours, the seasons, flights and altitude acclimatization."
---

## Bolivia and Brazil: two contrasting natural worlds

In Brazil, encounters with nature often begin beside the ocean, on the wooded slopes of Rio de Janeiro and near Iguazu Falls. In Bolivia, travelers discover high-altitude expanses: Uyuni Salt Flat, colorful lagoons and the volcanic regions of the Altiplano. These landscapes can be combined on one journey if the order of countries, flights and changing climate are planned in advance.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Brazil, Bolivia and the theme of nature. Bear in mind that **these are extensive journeys across South America involving additional countries**, rather than ready-made routes restricted to these two. They include itineraries visiting Argentina, Chile and Peru, and some longer programs cover other destinations as well.

## From humid forest to high-altitude plateau

### Brazil: Iguazu and Rio's green mountains

[Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) provides one of South America's most striking waterscapes. A broad stretch of waterfalls is surrounded by humid forest, with vegetation growing alongside paths and viewing walkways. Specific walking routes and access to viewpoints may change with weather and water conditions. Some itineraries also include the Argentine side of the falls, which is a separate visit involving border formalities.

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), nature shapes the city itself: bays, granite peaks, forests on the slopes and beaches. [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) helps explain why this metropolis is surrounded by so much greenery. However, a stop in Rio does not guarantee a separate walk through the national park; check the daily schedule of your chosen tour.

### Bolivia: white salt flats and colorful lakes

Around [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the vast ancient salt flat dominates the landscape. When dry, the white expanse stretches toward a distant mountain horizon. Following rain, a reflective layer of water appears in some areas. Photographs of a mirror-like surface depend on the weather and cannot be guaranteed in advance.

Southwestern Bolivia offers a different range of scenery. [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) stands out for the hues of its waters and its exposed volcanic surroundings; [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) sits among high mountains; and [the Salvador Dalí Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/) features unusual shapes in a rocky landscape. Some programs include [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and other stops across the highlands.

When comparing nature experiences, remember: **Iguazu means humid forest and a major river, while Uyuni is an exposed high-altitude landscape with dry air and cold nights**. This affects the season, what to pack and how comfortable the road journey will be.

## What is actually included in current itineraries

It is worth comparing several suitable options with different lengths and levels of activity:

| Tour | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| [5 Latin American countries in 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru on one journey |
| [6 Latin American countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | A broader itinerary from Rio and Iguazu to the Andes and Machu Picchu |
| [8 South American countries in 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | A long route with additional natural regions, including the Galápagos Islands |

On [the 18-day five-country journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the Brazilian leg covers Rio and Iguazu, while Bolivia offers lagoons and Uyuni. It is one way to experience both tropical and high-altitude nature within an existing comprehensive itinerary. Longer routes offer greater geographical variety but require more time for transfers and city visits.

If you would like to spend more days at natural sites, look beyond the name of the tour and the number of countries. Compare the day-by-day schedule and decide what matters most: independent walks, viewing platforms, excursions to lagoons or a broad overview of the continent.

## Seasons: where rain helps and where it gets in the way

Brazil and Bolivia have different environmental conditions even on the same dates. Iguazu can be visited throughout the year; the climate is especially humid in warmer months, and high water levels can restrict access to some walkways. Temperatures and humidity in Rio depend on the season and current weather, so visits to forested areas require their own forecast.

Around Uyuni, the rainy season changes the appearance of the salt flat: water creates reflections but can make certain areas difficult to drive through. During drier periods, the surface looks white and firm, although the highlands still have cold nights and intense sunlight.

It is better to select dates based on your priorities: **views of the waterfalls and comfortable walks**, or **a particular appearance of Uyuni and the ability to follow the planned route**. Both depend on conditions at the time. To avoid an overly ambitious plan, Ada Tours coordinates the order of stops and allows for weather-related changes, while access to individual areas is confirmed closer to departure.

## Planning flights and acclimatization

Rio and Uyuni are separated by great distances and very different elevations. Existing itineraries include other countries and intermediate stages between them. The key logistical questions are where flights are scheduled, where the route uses roads, how much time remains for rest, and how quickly the journey ascends.

Discuss acclimatization, exertion and any medical limitations well in advance of a visit to the Bolivian Altiplano. An excursion to a high-altitude lagoon can be physically more demanding than an ordinary city tour, even if most of the day is spent in a vehicle. The cold and dryness on the plateau feel especially pronounced after Brazil's humid heat.

Luggage must also suit two very different climates at once: light clothing and rain protection for Brazil, warmer layers, a windproof jacket and sun protection for Bolivia. Check baggage rules for the actual flights, especially if the itinerary uses small regional aircraft.

Travel documents must be checked for every country on the itinerary, not only Brazil and Bolivia. Visas, permitted transit and re-entry depend on nationality and the order of border crossings. Currencies differ too: Brazil uses the real and Bolivia the boliviano. Whether foreign cards work, currency exchange is available and payments can be made in remote areas needs separate confirmation. We help prepare a checklist tailored to the selected itinerary and type of journey.

## Who is this combination for?

This journey is particularly appealing to those who want to see contrasting landscapes on one holiday and are comfortable with an extended itinerary. A single trip can take you from forest and a mighty river to a salt flat and volcanic lakes, but this geographical range involves several transfers and adapting to changing altitude.

If you would prefer to focus on Bolivia's natural areas with fewer countries, explore [Bolivia destinations](/bolivia/) and discuss a private itinerary. For waterfalls and coastal scenery, see [Brazil](/brazil/). For a broader choice, explore [the Bolivia and Brazil combination](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil/) and [all multi-country nature journeys](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

When contacting Ada Tours, it is helpful to specify your desired natural sites, travel month and maximum trip length. This makes it possible to compare real programs rather than selecting a tour solely by the number of countries.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia and Brazil

### Are there ready-made tours covering only Bolivia and Brazil?

The current selection consists of itineraries that include both countries as well as other South American states. A journey limited to these two countries can be discussed separately as a private request.

### Can I combine Iguazu and Uyuni in one journey?

Yes, some existing comprehensive routes include both places. Remember that other countries, travel time and a major change in altitude are involved between these stages.

### Is the Uyuni mirror effect guaranteed in the rainy season?

No. A mirror-like surface appears when the water level is right, while rainfall can sometimes restrict driving. The purpose of the trip and the chosen season should be considered together.

### Which route should I choose for my first extensive South American journey?

Compare the 18- and 20-day itineraries by the number of transfers and stops at natural sites. A longer tour covers more regions but requires more time and energy. Giving priority to waterfalls, lagoons and salt flats is more useful than simply maximizing the number of countries.

lead: >-
  Nature experiences on journeys through Bolivia and Brazil are very different: humid Atlantic forest and Iguazu Falls give way to high-altitude lagoons, salt flats and the dry air of the Andes. In our current programs, these are stages of longer five- to eight-country routes, not a separate safari limited to two countries. We explain where nature stops are actually included, what you may see, and how to prepare for changes in climate and altitude.
---

## Nature in Bolivia and Brazil: which places are included in the itineraries?

The Brazilian and Bolivian parts of the journey offer two different ways to experience the natural world. Near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), you follow prepared walkways through humid forest, hear the waterfalls and take in the landscape from viewing platforms. In Bolivia, the main nature stages unfold in the highlands: around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Here travelers encounter mineral lakes, desert-like expanses and birds adapted to Altiplano conditions.

Our themed selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. **All matching programs cross more than two countries.** The mention of Bolivia and Brazil in the catalog title means both are part of the main route and wildlife watching is included somewhere in the full itinerary. In this selection, it is primarily associated with the Galápagos leg of the 32-day tour; the five- and six-country nature itineraries below are provided for comparison. It does not mean a continuous route limited to these two countries or guaranteed wildlife watching at every stop.

To explore the full geography without a thematic filter, see [tours through Bolivia and Brazil](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil/). For nature-oriented options, explore [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/) and [nature tours in Bolivia](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/).

## Brazil: waterfalls and tropical forest, not a guaranteed safari

One of the principal nature stops on these routes is the Brazilian side of Iguazu. At [the national park near Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the cascades, river valley and wooded slopes are the main attractions. Birds and other forest animals may be encountered, but a scheduled visit to the waterfalls does not automatically amount to a specialized wildlife-watching excursion.

For example, [the 18-day five-country group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) devotes a separate day to the Brazilian side of Iguazu. A visit to [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is mentioned as an optional possibility. If seeing birds is a priority, **check whether this visit is included in your chosen rate or needs to be added**. The fact that the bird park is close to the waterfalls does not mean its admission is included in every tour.

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the program generally focuses on the city, Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain. The green mountains and [Tijuca Forest](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) provide a natural backdrop, but an urban sightseeing excursion is a different experience from a trip dedicated to finding animals in the wild.

## Bolivia: lagoons, high-altitude birds and the salt flat

The Bolivian stages of the longer tours are much farther from urban infrastructure. On [the 18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), one stretch takes travelers in 4×4 vehicles past Laguna Verde, geothermal fields and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) before continuing to [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). These lagoons provide habitat for high-altitude birds, including flamingos. **A sighting of a particular species or the chance to get close is not guaranteed**: the birds move freely, and viewing conditions change.

The trip is also interesting for the contrast between ecosystems. Iguazu has humid vegetation and a powerful river; Uyuni is an open salt flat; around Laguna Colorada are cold winds, rocky shores and sparse high-altitude vegetation. Photographers will benefit from protection against dust and sun, while travelers need clothes for rapid temperature changes.

There is also an important practical point: the transition from lowland Brazil to high-altitude Bolivia usually runs through Chile and the [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) area. On the 18-day itinerary, a stop for acclimatization is planned before the journey to Uyuni. This matters especially to anyone sensitive to altitude: pace, overnight stays and physical exertion should be discussed before departure.

## Comparing Ada Tours itineraries

Programs vary in length and geography. The five- and six-country tours belong to the "Nature" theme; the eight-country itinerary additionally includes "Wildlife and Safaris" thanks to the excursions on the Galápagos Islands.

| Route | What it adds |
|---|---|
| 5 countries, 18 days | Iguazu, Atacama, Uyuni, Peru |
| 6 countries, 20 days | Montevideo and a route through the Andes |
| 8 countries, 32 days | Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia |

[The 18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) links Rio, Iguazu, Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni with Machu Picchu. ## Weather, altitude and limitations on nature visits

Tropical Brazil calls for lightweight clothing and rain protection, while high-altitude Bolivia requires warm layers and protection from the sun and wind. It may be cold at altitude even after a hot day in the previous country. Short visits to lagoons may offer little flexibility to rearrange the schedule if you feel unwell; it is best to address acclimatization before departure.

Water levels at Iguazu affect access to some viewing walkways, while weather and road conditions on the Altiplano may change driving times. Confirm individual visits and the availability of optional stops against the current itinerary, and check entry rules and medical advice for your citizenship and health circumstances.

### Can I see tropical forest and high-altitude lagoons on one journey?

Yes. On current longer itineraries, Brazil includes a stop at Iguazu, while Bolivia offers a journey to the lagoons and Uyuni. Other countries, transfers and changes in altitude lie between them.

### Is flamingo watching included?

The programs visit natural regions of Bolivia where high-altitude birds occur. A dedicated flamingo-watching excursion or a guaranteed sighting cannot be inferred from the tour title alone. Check the specific days and conditions.

### Is this selection suitable for visiting only Bolivia and Brazil?

Matching tours currently also include other main countries. A journey restricted to these two would require a separately planned itinerary; for comparing current tours, use [the general Bolivia + Brazil selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil/).

### How does the nature of Iguazu differ from Uyuni?

Iguazu means humid forest, a large river and waterfalls; Uyuni and nearby lagoons are high-altitude salt and mineral landscapes. Their climate, elevation, transport and the ways you experience them all differ.

## Bolivia, Brazil and Chile: from the ocean to the high-altitude desert

Travelers choose this combination for its contrasts. In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), you can see Guanabara Bay, granite mountains and Atlantic beaches. At [Iguazu Falls on the Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the journey continues among humid subtropical forests. A few days later, the route passes through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The air, the temperature and even your usual walking pace all change.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which **Brazil, Chile and Bolivia are part of the main itinerary**. At present these are five-country programs: Brazil → Argentina → Chile → Bolivia → Peru. Selecting three names in the catalog does not turn these journeys into self-contained three-country tours. Argentina and Peru remain full components of each program.

On [the 18-day group journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Rio and Iguazu are followed by Buenos Aires, Santiago, Atacama, the lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz before the Peruvian segment begins. [The private Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) adds a festival date in Rio, while [the 19-day New Year journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) begins with celebrations on Copacabana.

## Brazil: the start of the journey and tropical conditions

[Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) comes first on the published itineraries. Travelers explore the city, see Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado, then fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Humidity by the ocean and waterfalls is generally much higher than on the later Chilean and Bolivian stages.

Beachwear, lightweight clothing and sun protection are useful in Rio, but should not determine your entire packing list. Near Iguazu, protection from spray and rain is important, and shoes must cope with wet paths. Water may splash onto belongings even on a fine day.

**Do not assume that the move from Brazil to Chile is a single direct transfer.** The actual tours visit [the Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), from where a flight goes to Santiago. Argentina can only be added or removed from a private itinerary after flights and border crossings have been calculated afresh.

## Chile: Santiago, Calama and the arid Atacama

After Argentina, the route reaches [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a major city with its own sightseeing program. To reach the desert, travelers fly to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The apparently short distance on the map between San Pedro and the Bolivian lagoons is deceptive: the altitude rises sharply, and ordinary paved roads give way to remote highland stretches.

In Atacama, the sun can be strong by day, followed by a rapid drop in temperature after sunset. The difference between Santiago's climate and the high-altitude sites on the Bolivian border is particularly striking. Bring sunglasses, a hat, layered clothing and a windproof jacket. For an early departure, prepare warm clothes in advance rather than searching for them in the luggage compartment at the border.

On **entry into Chile**, all travelers must follow the agricultural rules of SAG. Plant and animal products carried in luggage must be declared in accordance with the official requirements. Nuts, fruit, meat products and souvenirs containing organic materials should be checked before flying from Argentina; a Chilean inspector makes the final decision on admission. Depending on the crossing, the declaration may be completed digitally or on paper.

## Chile–Bolivia crossing: the most sensitive hours of the itinerary

The route between [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and Bolivia's [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) runs through a high-altitude border zone. One official crossing in this area is **Hito Cajón**. According to Chile's border-crossing authority, the complex lies at approximately **4,549 m** and serves cars and minibuses. The actual crossing point, vehicle permissions and opening hours must be confirmed for the tour dates.

Our programs involve switching to the Bolivian road segment in **4×4 vehicles**. After crossing the border, travelers see Laguna Verde, geothermal areas and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). This is not an excursion you can comfortably undertake straight after a city walk without preparation. At altitude, cold, dry air and even modest physical activity can be tiring.

When coordinating the itinerary, we help check the border segment, transport arrangements, baggage and departure time. Extra time is needed for document checks and possible changes to road conditions. A precise border-crossing time should not be tied to a non-refundable flight departing on the same day.

## Bolivia: Uyuni, La Paz and the risks of rapid ascent

The high-altitude route leads to [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), then [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). The white salt flat, colorful lagoons and archaeological sites offer different experiences, so decide which segment matters most to you.

During the dry season, some parts of the salt flat are easier to drive across; during the rainy months, water may create a mirror effect but simultaneously restrict access to certain locations. Neither a particular surface appearance nor a specific jeep route can be guaranteed for every date. Trips during the Southern Hemisphere's summer rains require particularly careful planning.

Altitude sickness is related primarily to elevation and the speed of ascent, not athletic fitness. US CDC travel guidance recommends gaining altitude gradually when possible and allowing time to acclimatize. Continuing to ascend when symptoms worsen substantially is dangerous; discuss the appropriate response with a medical professional. A pre-trip consultation is especially important for travelers with heart or lung conditions.

**Insurance** should match the itinerary: check altitude limits, evacuation cover and overland travel in remote areas. Booking a standard sightseeing program does not mean that every policy covers such conditions.

## When to go and how to pack for three climate zones

There is no single month with "perfect" weather throughout this journey. Summer in the Southern Hemisphere coincides with festive periods in Rio, but it may also bring rain to high-altitude Bolivia. Santiago is often warm at that time, while Atacama can still be cold after sunset. In other months, freezing highland nights, wind and road conditions become important.

| Segment | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Heat, humidity and downpours |
| Santiago and Calama | City flights and dry climate |
| Atacama to the lagoons | Sun, cold and high altitude |
| Uyuni and La Paz | Acclimatization and seasonal road conditions |

Pack several layers that can be combined rather than heavy city clothes for the whole trip. Check baggage allowances separately for each domestic flight. Small aircraft, regional flights and ground transport may have different limits; an oversized suitcase will complicate the transition to the four-wheel-drive leg.

## Visas for Russian citizens and checks at every border

**As of October 15, 2026**, official Russian consular materials confirm visa-free entry for Russian citizens holding valid international passports on ordinary tourist visits to **Brazil, Chile and Bolivia**, for **up to 90 days within the applicable 180-day period**. These are separate agreements with three states, not a common immigration area.

On the actual five-country itineraries, you must also check entry to Argentina and Peru, air-transit requirements and each traveler's documents. A border officer considers the individual circumstances, including the purpose and duration of travel. Where an itinerary enters a country twice, previously spent days must also be taken into account. We help plan the document checks and crossing sequence but cannot guarantee a border authority's decision.

Check passport validity, insurance documents, rules for transporting medication and requirements for minors before buying separate non-refundable tickets. Visa conditions may be entirely different for other nationalities.

## Reais, pesos and bolivianos: expenses by segment

In Brazil, payments are in **reais (BRL)**; in Chile, **Chilean pesos (CLP)**; and in Bolivia, **bolivianos (BOB)**. On an existing five-country tour, you must also consider payments in Argentina (ARS) and Peru (PEN). US dollars may be useful for exchange but do not replace local currency for small purchases.

Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard bank cards do not work through international payment networks abroad. Any foreign card should be checked beforehand by country, currency, fees and bank restrictions; it is wise to distribute backup cash before the remote Bolivian leg. Even in major cities, acceptance of a particular card at every terminal cannot be guaranteed.

When comparing [four- and five-country journeys](/multi-country/), check what the chosen tour includes: domestic flights, admission tickets, meals, guide services and transfers. The labels "VIP" or "private" alone do not establish the service package. We help discuss likely payments and a practical cash reserve for each stage.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a ready-made tour limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Chile?

Here you will find trips that include these three countries on their main itinerary. Our current programs also cover Argentina and Peru. A journey limited to the three selected countries would need to be designed separately.

### Which direction do the existing itineraries follow?

They begin in Brazil and Iguazu, continue through Argentina and Chile with Santiago and Atacama, then Bolivia, and finally Peru. This order is essential for flights and the transition from Atacama to the lagoons.

### Can I travel directly from Atacama into Bolivia without a flight?

On the current itinerary, the segment after San Pedro de Atacama involves an overland border crossing followed by travel through Bolivia in 4×4 vehicles. The chosen border post, transport and road conditions are checked for the departure date.

### Will the summer clothes I pack for Rio work for the whole tour?

No. Even during warmer months, the Bolivian highlands can have cold nights and strong winds. Bring warm layers and protection from wind, sun and possible rain.

### Should I worry about altitude even without difficult climbs?

Yes. High altitude affects ordinary sightseeing travelers as well. Consider your rate of ascent, physical condition, medical contraindications and insurance coverage even if your walks are short.
